speaker: Sheldon
text: What? I have good news. Your cell phone was off.

speaker: Leonard
text: And you had to barge in here and wake us up in the middle of the night? Because we didn't want to be disturbed.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, that didn't work out, did it?

speaker: Leonard
text: Sheldon, what do you want?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I came to tell you, I've got the answer.

speaker: Leonard
text: Really? You figured out the graphene problem?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, well, I'm still hopelessly stuck on that, but I figured out how to figure it out.

speaker: Leonard
text: Hey, you know, Leonard, I know I said I could handle your roommate, but I was wrong. We're gonna have to break up.

speaker: Sheldon
text: What are you talking about? Einstein.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, I'm gonna need a little more.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Albert Einstein.

speaker: Leonard
text: Keep going.

speaker: Sheldon
text: When Albert Einstein came up with special relativity, he was working at the patent office.

speaker: Leonard
text: So, you're gonna go work at the patent office?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Don't be absurd. That's in Washington. You know I could never live in a city. The streets are laid out in a wheel and spoke pattern.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm going to find a similarly menial job where my basal ganglia are occupied with a routine task, freeing my prefrontal cortex to work quietly in the background on my problem.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sounds like a great plan.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Of course it is. Even talking to you is sufficiently menial that I can feel the proverbial juices starting to flow.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay, well, thanks for sharing with us. Good night.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You're welcome. Good night to you, too. By the way, I was watching you sleep for a moment, and I noticed that your snoring seems to be worse when you're on your back.

speaker: Leonard
text: Leonard doesn't snore.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, I wasn't talking to Leonard.
